decisions.rationale: Lead Charizard and Torkoal to immediately establish the Drought + Heat Rock sun core, enabling Charizard-Mega-Y and Venusaur's Chlorophyll speed. Back Venusaur as the primary sun sweeper with Growth-boosted Giga Drain/Sludge Bomb, and Aegislash to wall opposing Psychic and Dragon types (Farigiraf, Armarouge) while providing flinch pressure via Sacred Sword and King's Rock.

Meowscarada and Skarmory remain as flexible pivots for mid-game cleaning and hazard stacking respectively. Prioritize getting sun up turn 1 and protecting Torkoal to extend it to 8 turns.

decisions.rationale: Lead Altaria and Mamoswine to suppress opposing sun, establish Tailwind, and immediately threaten Charizard, Torkoal, and Flying types with Rock Slide. Armarouge provides Wide Guard against spread Fire attacks, while Archaludon supplies powerful special coverage into the opponent's Fire- and Flying-heavy roster.
decisions.notebook: Preferred core is Altaria plus Mamoswine with Armarouge and Archaludon in reserve; preserve Cloud Nine and Tailwind when possible, and use Armarouge's Wide Guard to answer spread Fire pressure.

decisions.rationale: Charizard's Fire Blast is 2x super-effective against Mamoswine, the most dangerous foe due to Rock Slide's 4x threat to Charizard and High Horsepower's 2x threat to Torkoal. Eliminating Mamoswine early is the highest priority. Torkoal uses Protect to avoid damage this turn, preserving its HP to maintain Drought ability for sun extension across future turns. Mega Evolution is not needed since sun is already active from Torkoal's Drought on entry, and Mega-Y's Speed drop from 167 to ~100 would sacrifice Charizard's key speed advantage.

decisions.rationale: Prioritize eliminating Mamoswine (notebook priority target). Charizard's Solar Beam (Grass, 120 BP) is 2x super-effective vs Mamoswine's Ground typing and fires with no charge turn under active sun—outclassing Focus Blast (70% accuracy) and Fire Blast (neutralized to 1x by Thick Fat). Torkoal's Earth Power (Ground, 90 BP) is also 2x super-effective vs Mamoswine's Ice typing with perfect accuracy. Hitting Mamoswine with two simultaneous SE moves maximizes KO probability and removes the Pokemon threatening both active team members with Rock Slide (4x vs Charizard) and High Horsepower (2x vs Torkoal).

reflections.summary: The sweep package (Charizard, Venusaur) was dismantled before it could function — Mamoswine's Rock Slide/Icicle Crash eliminated both Charizard and Venusaur by turn 3, both super-effective and aided by Altaria's Helping Hand. Torkoal Body-Pressed for useful chip but also fell to Rock Slide. Aegislash successfully cleaned Mamoswine on turn 4, but with only one Pokémon remaining against Altaria plus Armarouge (and an unrevealed third), there was no staying power left. Altaria's Focus Sash + Helping Hand + Tailwind made Mamoswine nearly unbreakable early, and the team lacked a defensive backbone once the sun sweepers were gone.
reflections.adjustment: Replace one of the redundant sun setters or the fragile Venusaur slot with a physically bulky pivot or a dedicated Altaria/Mamoswine check (e.g., Skarmory to threaten Altaria's sash and absorb Rock Slides, or Meowscarada for speed-tier revenge killing under sun). The team needs at least one durable member that can survive Mamoswine's coverage after Helping Hand and still threaten back.
reflections.notebook: Opponent Altaria runs Focus Sash / Cloud Nine / Helping Hand — must be removed turn 1 or it enables Mamoswine relentlessly. Mamoswine carries Rock Slide (widespread super-effective coverage) and Icicle Crash; ThickFat + ExpertBelt makes it bulky and hard to break without super-effective priority or special attacks. Armarouge is a special attacker with Armor Cannon (FlashFire); modest and quiet, likely the 4th slot. Sun team over-invested in weather redundancy (Charizard Y + Torkoal) leaving only two offensive slots that were too frail to survive Helping Hand-boosted neutral hits. Next game: bring one reliable sun setter, one bulky pivot or defensive check, keep one fast sweeper, and one wallbreaker. Skarmory and Meowscarada remain strong flexible pivots to test.

reflections.summary: Won through an excellent anti-sun plan: Cloud Nine Altaria removed the weather advantage, Tailwind plus Helping Hand enabled Mamoswine to eliminate Charizard, Venusaur, and Torkoal quickly, and the back line finished Aegislash. Piloting was clean with no recorded decision errors. The four brought were well suited to this opponent; no Mega Stone holder was available or evolved, which was appropriate for this roster.
reflections.adjustment: After Mamoswine secures an early knockout, avoid leaving it exposed to Aegislash's physical pressure. Transition sooner to Armarouge or Archaludon to handle Aegislash while preserving Mamoswine for remaining sun threats.
reflections.notebook: Opponent's revealed primary mode is Charizard-Y/Torkoal sun with Chlorophyll Venusaur; Cloud Nine, Tailwind, and fast spread pressure are effective counterplay. Aegislash is a physical attacker carrying Sacred Sword, Shadow Sneak, King's Shield, and Swords Dance, so preserve a dedicated answer rather than relying on Mamoswine into it. Armarouge remains the preferred Wide Guard answer to opposing spread Fire attacks; preserve it when feasible. Continue prioritizing anti-sun leads and use Mamoswine's pressure to force early KOs before pivoting it out of Aegislash matchups.
